_comment: Frozen run config for the six mix_scale_* budget points (2026-08-30). One file, not six copies: the six points must differ only in D. `harness run point` reads this and refuses a disagreeing CLI flag; check_ladder_config compares every ladder checkpoint's cfg against it. A change to any value reopens the whole ladder. Two kinds of fields: (1) CLI-settable (_FROZEN_KEYS) — every Cfg field with a CLI flag that changes the architecture or the recipe, excluding seed; check_frozen_keys_complete enforces this against train.py's parser. (2) Code-only (_CODE_FROZEN_KEYS) — architecture constants with no CLI flag, recorded as documented intent so a code edit before the first point diverges from a recorded value and fails. chunk_size is a code constant (Cfg.chunk_size=32, no CLI flag); NCCL protocol is default. Bool fields match Cfg defaults, so no flag is needed to achieve them — _strip_frozen refuses a flag that would change one. See docs/standards/0830v1_gates.md. SPLIT 2026-08-30: `world` is the RECIPE (card count changes the effective batch and the gradient noise, so it changes the optimisation); `cards` is the ALLOCATION (which H20s, which changes no computation). They were one string, and NGPU was split out of it, so editing the list to dodge a busy card silently changed the count with nothing raising. run point now asserts len(cards) == world and that every named card is idle. `world` is deliberately in NEITHER frozen-key tuple: train.py does not stamp it into a checkpoint's cfg, so comparing it there would report UNKNOWN forever -- it is enforced at the launch gate, which is the only place it can actually be checked today. REALLOCATED 2026-08-30: cards 1-7 -> 0-6, world still 7. This is the allocation half moving and the recipe half standing still, which is the whole reason they were split: eight H20s are identical and any seven span the same NVSwitch domain, so card IDENTITY changes no computation. GPU 0 being the bench lane is an operating convention, not part of the recipe. The six ladder points ran on 1-7 and stay comparable. WARMDOWN/ANNEAL_FRAC ADDED 2026-09-01: 8199ee0 put both into _FROZEN_KEYS and did not add them here, so frozen[k] raised KeyError and check_ladder_config died before checking ANY key -- the crash was mistaken for the check running, and the other 20 keys went unverified from 8/31 16:15. Values are train.py Cfg defaults (0.65, 0.10), read from the source rather than chosen: every ladder point ran without a flag for either, so those are the values the six points DID run. This records what happened; it does not decide what the 500M run should run -- a stage-1 WSD join wants warmdown=0 and anneal_frac=0, which is the launch owner's recipe decision. The rule above guards a CHANGE to a value, not a RECORD of the value that ran (fb ruling 2026-09-01). conv_doc_isolated is recorded FALSE, which is what these six points actually trained with and not a preference: before 2026-09-04 the KDA short_conv was applied to the whole row and never saw cu, so documents were not isolated inside it (eff.kda_document_isolation_violated). The flag exists to fix that for NEW runs; recording false here freezes the ladder as it ran, so a point re-run under the fix diverges from this file and fails rather than quietly comparing two topologies. MEM_* ADDED 2026-09-05: the four sparse-memory keys went into _FROZEN_KEYS with the memory layer, and this file is where a frozen key acquires a value -- omitting them is the warmdown/anneal_frac failure again, where the absent-key branch fails the whole check and the other keys stop being verified. Values are train.py Cfg defaults, read from the source rather than chosen: mem_values 0 means no memory pool, which is what the six points ran, and with it 0 the other three are inert (HybridLM builds no ProductKeyMemory at all, model.py:654). So this records the ladder as it ran and does not decide anything for the memory arms -- those are NOT ladder points: they launch off the head-hybrid control's line, their mix is not a mix_scale_* one, and _is_ladder_mix excludes them from this comparison. The six existing ladder checkpoints predate the fields entirely, so their cfg carries no key and they report as `unverifiable (pre-stamp)` rather than as a mismatch, which is the correct reading: the field did not exist when they trained.
